Beyond Attention Maps:Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs
via Visual Values

Yichen Zhao1,2,3 *Fenghe Tang1,2,3 *Wenxin Ma4Rongsheng Wang1,2,3Zihao Wan1,2,3Shaohua Kevin Zhou1,2,3 †

arχivPaperCode🤗Data

Abstract

Where a medical MLLM attends does not fully explain what it understands. Using paired non-contrast (NC) and contrast-enhanced (CE) scans, we find similar attention maps can yield different answers, while interventions on visual values have a stronger effect on predictions than interventions on attention weights. We propose VIVID (VIsual Value Intervention Distillation), which uses CE visual values to refine teacher corrections for on-policy distillation. VIVID improves medical VQA across six internal and external test sets, while requiring only NC images at inference.

Observation

Similar attention maps, different answers. Paired NC and CE scans show highly similar attention maps, yet produce different predictions of tumor multiplicity.

KEY INSIGHT

What is read matters beyond where to attend. Transferring CE visual values has a stronger effect on predictions than transferring attention maps. Even with noisy attention maps after value replacement, the overall gains remain larger than those from attention-map replacement.

Method

VIVID mixes CE visual values into an auxiliary branch and uses the induced prediction shift to refine distillation targets.

Main Results

VIVID improves over the compared training baselines on both internal and external test sets across liver, brain, and breast VQA.
